Name: Faction_JerusalemChurch
Description: The mother congregation, led by Peter and then by James the Lord's brother. Observant of the Law, Aramaic-speaking, and under steady pressure from the Temple authorities.

Name: Faction_HellenistBelievers
Description: Greek-speaking Jewish believers, scattered from Jerusalem after Stephen's death and the first to carry the message beyond Judaea.

Name: Faction_GentileBelievers
Description: Congregations of non-Jews, from Cornelius onward. Their standing in the movement is the live question of Acts 15 and of Galatians.

Name: Faction_PhariseeParty
Description: Rigorous interpreters of the Law with wide popular support. Divided about the movement: some of its members join it, and Gamaliel counsels leaving it alone.

Name: Faction_TempleEstablishment
Description: The chief priests and the Sadducean aristocracy who run the Temple and hold their position at Rome's pleasure. They deny the resurrection as a doctrine, which makes the movement's central claim intolerable.

Name: Faction_ZealotsSicarii
Description: Armed factions committed to expelling Rome, and to killing the Jews who collaborate with it. They regard the movement's refusal to take up the cause as desertion.

Name: Faction_RomanAdministration
Description: Prefects, procurators and proconsuls, and the auxiliaries who enforce them. Indifferent to doctrine and intensely interested in public order.

Name: Faction_HerodianClients
Description: Agrippa I and his successors, ruling at Rome's sufferance and needing to be seen keeping their own house in order.

Name: Faction_DiasporaSynagogues
Description: Jewish communities from Damascus to Rome, each with its own leadership. The first place any travelling preacher goes, and often the first place he is thrown out of.

Name: Faction_PaganCivicCults
Description: Temple priesthoods, trade guilds and civic festivals across the Greek cities. Their objection is rarely theological and usually economic, as the Ephesian silversmiths demonstrate.

Name: Faction_GnosticTeachers
Description: Second-century schools offering a saving knowledge above the public account, and generally embarrassed by the claim that God took a body. Opponents in argument rather than in arms.

Name: Faction_Marcionites
Description: Followers of Marcion, who cut the Hebrew scriptures away from the movement and kept an edited Luke and a shortened Paul. The first group to force the question of which writings belong.
